title: Finance & Legal Operational Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, RevRec and Billing (Q1 2026)
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference	 s operational guidance for budgeting & forecasting, contracts and legal processes, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition & billing for Q1 2026. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, sales, and product leaders who own planning, contracting, and month-end operations.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood entities that book revenue, sign vendor/customer contracts, or place procurement orders.
- Does not replace legal review for non-standard contract terms or capital expenditures > $250k (see Escalation).

1) Budgeting & Forecasting

Purpose: Provide a repeatable, auditable process to produce quarterly and annual forecasts that drive capacity planning, hiring, and sales quotas.

Cadence and Owners:
- Annual operating plan (AOP): Finance (lead: FP&A Manager) compiles inputs from Product, Eng, Growth, and Sales. Final AOP due to CFO by 2025-11-30.
- Quarterly re-forecast: Rolling 12-month view updated monthly; consolidated forecast published by the 10th business day each month. Owner: FP&A.
- Monthly variance analysis: Finance produces actual vs. forecast variance report within five business days of month close.

Forecasting methodology:
1. Bottom-up bookings model (Sales Owned)
   - Inputs: open pipeline by stage, historical conversion rates, weighted ARR by close probability.
   - Conversion assumptions versioned and stored in the Forecast workbook (Finance S3 / shared drive).
2. Usage-driven revenue model (Platform Owned)
   - Inputs: active user count, avg tokens/embedding units, model mix, price per unit.
   - Key metric: tokens per active user per month (baseline: 12M tokens/user/month for hosted customers).
3. Expense model (Functional Owners)
   - Ops: infrastructure, cloud/GPU costs by instance type and region.
   - R&D: headcount-driven, with burdened cost rates published quarterly.

Forecast controls and thresholds:
- Materiality threshold: Any forecast variance > 5% of quarterly revenue requires a written variance memo and leadership review.
- Hiring freeze trigger: if 12-month cash runway falls below 9 months, hiring approvals require CFO sign-off.
- CapEx approval: any single CapEx > $250,000 requires CFO + Head of Eng approval; > $1,000,000 requires CEO.

Deliverables and templates:
- Monthly Forecast Workbook (single source of truth) \u2014 template in /finance/templates/monthly-forecast.xlsx
- Variance Memo template \u2014 see Appendix A

2) Contracts & Legal Process

Objective: Standardize contracting lifecycle to reduce risk, accelerate close velocity, and ensure consistent revenue recognition triggers.

Contract lifecycle steps:
1. Opportunity qualification: Sales attaches standard SOW template and expected billing cadence to opportunity record.
2. Legal intake: SalesOps files contract request in Contract Intake tracker with key commercial terms.
3. Legal review: Legal team performs redline review using standard playbook. Non-standard terms trigger Legal + Finance review.
4. Signature & storage: Fully executed contracts uploaded to Contract Repository (DocuSign + Box) and indexed with metadata (customer, effective_date, term, MRR, contract_type).

Standard contract types and owners:
- Standard SaaS Subscription Agreement: Sales + Legal (auto-approve if discounts < 25% and contract term <= 24 months).
- Enterprise Contract / Custom SOW: Legal + Finance review required for revenue recognition and billing setup.
- Reseller / Partner Agreement: Partnerships + Legal; revenue recognition varies by principal vs agent determination.

Key contract controls:
- Discount approval matrix: discounts > 25% require VP Sales + Finance approval; > 50% require CRO + CFO.
- SOC2/Privacy Addendum: Required for customers requesting data residency or custom security terms (Legal owner).
- Contract metadata completeness: Contracts missing MRR, start_date or term are flagged by Finance and put on hold for billing until metadata is corrected.

Retention and auditability:
- All contracts retained for minimum 7 years (Legal), with indexed full-text search in the Contract Repository.
- Quarterly contract audit: Legal + Finance run a sample of 20 contracts to confirm metadata accuracy and revenue treatment.

3) Procurement Procedures

Goal: Ensure procurement is compliant, cost-efficient, and auditable while maintaining velocity for critical purchases (cloud, GPUs, vendor services).

Procurement request flow:
1. Requisition: Requestor opens a purchase request in ProcureFlow with business justification and cost center.
2. Approval routing: Automated routing based on amount per matrix below.
3. PO issuance: Procurement issues PO and records vendor W-9/TIN and master services agreement (MSA) where required.
4. Receipt and invoice match: AP matches invoices to PO and enters into the ERP for payment.

Approval matrix:
- <= $5,000: Manager approval (functional).
- $5,001 - $50,000: Director approval + Procurement review.
- $50,001 - $250,000: VP approval + Procurement + Finance.
- > $250,000: Finance + Procurement + CFO + Legal (if contract required).

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Vendor questionnaire completed (security/privacy) \u2014 required for any vendor with access to customer data.
- MSA signed for recurring services (legal owner).
- Tax forms collected (W-9 / W-8BEN) \u2014 Finance owner.
- Payment terms standardized: net 30 unless vendor provides early-payment discount options that exceed finance hurdle rate.

Preferred procurement categories and owners:
- Cloud & GPU Instances: Eng Infra + Procurement (annual reserved commitments centrally negotiated).
- Professional Services (SIs): Product + Legal + Procurement.
- SaaS Tools: IT Procurement + Security review for access to sensitive data.

Emergency procurement (fast lanes):
- For purchases required to mitigate active incidents (severity P0/P1), Eng Ops owner can request an emergency PO. Emergency POs require post-facto review and documented justification.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Objective: Ensure consistent ASC 606-compliant revenue recognition and predictable invoicing for customers.

Revenue recognition principles (summary):
- Revenue recognized when control of promised goods or services is transferred to the customer in an amount that reflects the consideration Redwood expects to be entitled to.
- Revenue is allocated to performance obligations in the contract. Typical obligations: hosted API usage, dedicated capacity reservation, private deployment license, and professional services.

Typical treatments:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (over time) \u2014 invoiced monthly in arrears.
- Dedicated / Reserved capacity (committed ARR): Recognize ratably over the contract term (monthly recognition for annual prepayments).
- Private deployment (license + support): License component: evaluate for distinct performance obligation; if non-transferable, recognize over contract term per the delivery schedule.
- Professional services: Recognize based on percentage-of-completion or milestone accounting depending on contract terms and acceptance criteria.

Billing cadence and invoicing:
- Standard: Monthly invoices for usage and recurring charges. Payment terms: Net 30 (unless customer-specific negotiated terms exist).
- Annual prepayments: Invoice on signature; recognition ratable unless criteria for upfront recognition are met.
- Late payments: Interest charged at 1.5% per month after 30 days; accounts > 60 days delinquent escalated to Sales Ops + Customer Success.

Billing system setup checklist (Finance Ops):
- Confirm customer legal entity and billing address.
- Confirm contract metadata: start_date, term, renewal_terms, MRR, billing_frequency, performance_obligations.
- Configure tax treatment: SaaS sales tax/VAT rules per customer jurisdiction (Tax owner: Finance Tax Manager).

Credit/Refunds/Adjustments:
- Credit notes issued for clear billing errors only (Finance & Sales Ops approval).
- Refunds require CFO approval for amounts > $10,000 or where refund materially impacts quarter revenue.

Automation and controls:
- Billing automation owner: Finance Systems (Stripe/Zuora sync + ERP). All invoices must be reconciled to the general ledger daily.
- Revenue waterfall: Monthly automated P&L posting process to ensure consistent recognition across product lines.

5) Month-end Close Checklist (Finance Ops)

Timebox: Close should be completed within 5 business days of month-end for reporting; extended close (sub-ledgers, tax accruals) within 10 business days.

Top tasks:
1. Invoice run and AR posting (Day +1).
2. Bank reconciliation (Day +2).
3. Accruals for usage-based revenue (Day +2).
4. Review of deferred revenue roll-forwards (Day +3).
5. Fixed asset & CapEx posting (Day +3).
6. FX revaluation and tax accruals (Day +4).
7. Final P&L and variance commentary (Day +5).

Close controls:
- All manual journal entries > $25,000 require supporting documentation and Manager approval.
- Sizable cutoffs (> $50,000) flagged and require Controller sign-off.

6) Ownership, Escalations and SLAs

Primary owners:
- FP&A & Forecasting: Director of FP&A (owner).
- Contracts & Legal Intake: Head of Legal (owner).
- Procurement: Head of Procurement (owner).
- Billing & RevRec: Controller (owner).
- Billing system reliability SLO: 99.9% uptime for invoice generation and delivery systems (Finance Systems team).

Escalation paths:
- Contract with non-standard legal terms or > $250k: escalate to Head of Legal + CFO within 24 hours of intake.
- Procurement disputes > $50k: Procurement Lead + Finance within 48 hours.
- Revenue recognition accounting uncertainty (ASC 606 judgement): Controller + External audit partner consult within 72 hours.

7) Compliance, Audit & Record Retention

- Audit readiness: Quarter-end close kits retained for 3 years; contract and billing records retained for 7 years.
- SOC2 evidence: Procurement and vendor onboarding artefacts must be available for SOC auditors on request.

- Monthly Forecast Workbook: /finance/templates/monthly-forecast.xlsx
- Contract Intake Form: /legal/templates/contract-intake.xlsx
- Variance Memo Template: /finance/templates/variance-memo.docx
- Procurement Requisition: /procurement/templates/requisition-form.xlsx

Appendix B: Example Journal Entries (text)
- Deferred revenue recognition for annual prepaid Dedicated contract (invoice $120,000 on 2026-01-01, 12-month term):
  - Dr Cash $120,000
  - Cr Deferred Revenue $120,000
  - Monthly recognition (Jan): Dr Deferred Revenue $10,000; Cr Revenue $10,000
